what: Seven killed after teen shooter opens fire at home and school in Thailand

clean_source_blocks.text: Police have been combing over the school for evidence At least seven people have been killed and 23 injured after a 14-year-old boy opened fire at his home and school on the outskirts of Thailand's capital Bangkok. The gunman - a student at the Debsirin School in Nonthaburi - killed his grandparents and five teachers before taking his own life, Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul told reporters. The attacker still had "more than 30 bullets left" when he turned the gun on himself, Anutin added. Nine of the injured people remain in a critical condition, authorities say. The shooting - the second at a school in Thailand this year - has renewed pressure on the government for greater action on gun control.
Authorities say the 14-year-old killed his grandparents before gunning down five teachers at his school.

Thai police say that a 14-year-old boy killed two of his grandparents at their home using a handgun belonging to his grandfather. The suspect then went to the Debsirin School, where he was a pupil, and opened fire. Amid conflicting reported casualty figures, police have said five teachers were shot at the school, before the suspect shot himself. At least 30 people were injured in the shooting, with at least nine of them believed to be severely wounded. Thailand’s prime minister Anutin Charnvirakul said the suspect was “under stress” and appeared to have planned the assault. Charnvirakul has vowed to propose ⁠a new law to restrict the carrying of firearms by the public, in a country which has one of the highest rates of private gun ownership in the world. The country has witnessed several mass shootings in recent years.

Police were deployed to the scene during the active shooting, which began just after 10:00 local time (03:00 GMT). National police chief police general Kittiratt Phanphet told reporters that forensic officers had found the gunman's shots were quite accurate, with several hitting vital spots on the body. The prime minister said the attack was "well prepared" with "clear steps and clear goals". The attacker has not been publicly named, and police haven't disclosed a motive - though the prime minister said the boy may have been stressed about his studies. Investigations are continuing, with officers seen carrying away computer equipment and boxes from the home the shooter shared with his grandparents, who he shot dead before the school rampage. The Debsirin School, founded in Bangkok in 1885, is one of Thailand's top secondary schools with branches across the country. It counts many prominent Thai figures as its alumni, from diplomats and athletes to several prime ministers.

A female seventh grader, still in school uniform, told the BBC she was standing in front of her teacher when the woman was shot.
